title: Pañcaślokī — Five Verses
author: Abhinavagupta
text:
The Pañcaślokī is a brief surrender-hymn of five verses by Abhinavagupta, preserved with the works gathered under the Abhinavastotrāvali. Its stance is stated without ornament: the whole of the devotee's duty is one act — pride laid at the Lord's feet, every other claim denied, and even immediate pleasure asked only from that source. Five verses are enough, because the doctrine needs no elaboration: sovereignty surrendered is the entire discipline.

Its juice: the poem's sharpness lies in what it refuses. Not a program, not a balance of duties — a single radical transfer of agency. Abhinavagupta writes as one who has already run out of alternatives worth keeping, and the five verses read like the last word on the matter rather than a first step.
